question: Which polhode-geometric scalar (D label, |D-1|, cone_max, pol_diam) predicts the s042 omega-mag basin width better than the trivial |omega| baseline?
hypothesis: A genuinely polhode-derived quantity predicts basin width; the s051 mechanism (near-separatrix D -> narrow basin) should make |D-1| the predictor.
narrative_md: Cohort polhode survey (100 seeds, 3.9 s) cross-correlated with the 10 s042 basin measurements: polhode DIAMETER is the load-bearing basin-width predictor (Spearman -0.935, p<0.001), stronger than |omega| (-0.837) and far stronger than the D label (+0.105, not correlated). This partially refutes s051 (D doesn't predict) but vindicates the polhode framing more sharply (pol_diam does). Cohort topology: 87/100 enclose I_c, 50/100 near-separatrix. Computes polhode invariants from truth (q0, omega0) of every cohort seed.
